items.title: Amazon turns its most capable smart speaker into a smart camera, too
items.rationale: New hardware: in its 10-28 Echo launch, Amazon added a camera to the Echo Studio for $30 more, so Alexa+ can 'see and understand' the room. This one card stands for the whole Echo/Alexa+ launch cluster.
items.excerpt: The Echo Studio with Home Camera can "see and understand what's in front of the camera."

items.title: Android XR's First AR Glasses 'XREAL Aura' Launch Today, Starting at $1,100 for Limited Time
items.rationale: New product on sale: XREAL Aura, the first AR glasses running Android XR with Gemini built in, ships today starting at $1,100.
items.excerpt: XREAL announced that XREAL AURA, the first AR glasses running Google's Android XR operating system, is launching today, starting at $1,100 for a limited time.

items.title: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs
items.rationale: New decision: Microsoft is removing its Copilot assistant from LG and Samsung smart TVs about two years after launch. It is a clear retreat of an AI assistant from a device category.
items.excerpt: Microsoft's AI assistant will soon disappear from your TV.

items.title: OpenAI now lets you text your Dot agent
items.rationale: New feature: OpenAI's proactive Dot agent can now be reached by iMessage and RCS, so it works inside the phone's default messaging app.
items.excerpt: The feature works with both iMessage and RCS messaging.

items.title: iOS 27.2: Apple's AI images now carry Google's SynthID watermark
items.rationale: New release behavior: in iOS 27.2, Apple embeds Google's invisible SynthID pixel watermark in Image Playground output and heavily edited photos. The mark is built to survive cropping and compression, which matters for anyone who publishes AI imagery.
items.excerpt: With iOS 27.2, Apple marks all images from Image Playground and more extensively edited photos with Google's invisible SynthID watermark. It is embedded in the pixels rather than the metadata and is designed to survive cropping and compression.

dedup.note: Amazon Echo/Alexa+ 10-28 launch (c0 aboutamazon + Digital Trends Home Map, c1 ZDNET + Ars Echo Studio camera, CNET Echo vs HomeView, CNET Echo Time, Engadget Alexa Photo Frame): all one launch event, so I kept only Ars (on the whitelist, and its AI-camera angle is the strongest). Its history_match, the 10-10 Verge 'one year with Alexa Plus' review, and the 10-09 Engadget Alexa tablets card are earlier, separate events. XREAL Aura (c9: Road to VR, Android Authority, blog.google): kept Road to VR for the price and ship date. The 10-17 Android Authority Gemini-on-XR teardown is a different story. Also dropped from the glasses group: the Samsung XR glasses 'doomed' opinion piece (commentary on the 10-14 Samsung reveal), the Engadget 'how to tell if someone uses AI glasses' explainer (evergreen), INMO GO3 (flagged sponsored on 10-26, and stale), and the Android XR dev tools item (second Android XR item on the same day; a developer story). Copilot on TVs (c20: Verge, XDA): kept the Verge. The 10-08 Copilot-in-Windows and 10-24 File Explorer cards are different events. OpenAI Dot (c7: Engadget, 9to5Mac): kept Engadget. The gadgets history has no earlier Dot card, and the history_match (Ollama TTS) is unrelated. SynthID: the nearest earlier card is the 10-27 9to5Mac 'what's new in iOS 27.2' Siri roundup, which is about Siri, not the watermark, so this one is new. Other drops: Gemini Live redesign sneak peek (an unreleased teardown, dropped 10-28 too); Gemini Notebook recorder (a small increment on the 10-25 Notebook card); Perplexity Mac voice mode (lower priority); Meta Waddle World (AI pet app, not a gadget); Japan chainsaw robot (still human-operated, so a demo). Cross-section: I had no grep tool, so I did NOT exact-grep published_urls.json. The orchestrator must verify these 5 URLs, plus 'Echo Studio', 'XREAL Aura', 'Dot' and 'SynthID', against every section. The SynthID item (10-27) is the most likely to clash with design or politics. Diversity: 5 outlets (Ars, Road to VR, The Verge, Engadget, Notebookcheck), each with a distinct accent.
